emily (customer): Hey team — since yesterday our p99 for streaming responses jumped from ~900ms to ~3.2s. Non-streaming calls are steady. Any ideas?

jess (support): Thanks for reporting — can you share a minimal repro request and whether you see the same on hosted vs dedicated?

emily (customer): Repro steps: curl to /v1/stream with SSE, model redwood-mini, prompt ~200 tokens, client waits for chunks. Happens on hosted.
emily (customer): Quick curl we used:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","input":"repeat word 150"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
jess (support): Got it. Two quick checks: 1) do you see consistent first-byte times? 2) are the long tails showing as gaps between chunks or long total times?
emily (customer): First chunk arrives fast ~150ms, then a few large gaps (~2–4s) before subsequent chunks. Looks like mid-stream pauses.
miguel (infra): Possible suspects: edge/proxy buffering, HTTP/2 flow-control, or intermediary resetting stream windows. Any chance they're hitting an intermediary like Cloudflare or corporate proxy?
emily (customer): They are on a corporate network but we repro from home too. Also tried both h2 and SSE and behavior is similar.
alex (eng-runtime): Can you paste headers you see from the response (esp: transfer-encoding, connection, keep-alive, x-env)? Also which client lib?
emily (customer): Using our internal Go client (net/http), headers snippet: `transfer-encoding: chunked`, `connection: keep-alive`, no x-env.
alex (eng-runtime): Ok. On the runtime side we recently rolled a change that disables small-chunk flush when a connection is detected as multiplexed behind certain proxies — to avoid small chunk amplification. That can introduce mid-stream coalescing on some paths.
jess (support): That sounds promising. Miguel — any proxy-level metrics around connection re-use or window updates around that time?
miguel (infra): Checking edge logs now. I see a pattern: when clients reuse a connection and we detect >1 concurrent streams, we coalesce flushes which can produce larger pauses for token-by-token streaming. p99 lines up with rollout times.
ops-bot: Deploy #deploy/runtime/2026-03-15 completed 2026-03-15T18:42:10Z (change: streaming-flush-coalesce v2)
miguel (infra): Confirmed: the deploy corresponds with spike window and customer p99.
alex (eng-runtime): Root cause: heuristic to avoid tiny chunk overhead merged last week. It reduces server-side CPU but increases chunk coalescing when connections are multiplexed. Some clients (esp. net/http with default transport or corp proxies) end up seeing big gaps.
jess (support): Short-term workaround for customers: set header `X-Redwood-Stream-Flush: aggressive` or fall back to non-streaming. Can we expose that?
alex (eng-runtime): We can toggle a compatibility header to force per-token flushing. I'll open a hotfix flag to re-enable fine-grained flush for hosted tier for the next 24h. Also add guidance: if client sits behind corporate proxies, recommend SSE over HTTP/2 or enable keepalive at 15s.
miguel (infra): I'll roll a targeted config change to revert the heuristic for affected edge regions and add a metric for chunk gap distribution (ms between chunks).
jess (support): Emily — would you like me to temporarily flip the header for your org so you can confirm?
emily (customer): Yes please, that would be great.
jess (support): Done — I pushed `X-Redwood-Stream-Flush: aggressive` for your org id. Can you retry and send logs?
emily (customer): Retrying now... first chunk 140ms, subsequent gaps ~200ms. p99 back to ~980ms. Looks fixed on our side. Huge thanks.
alex (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: 1) revert coalescing rollout and create a safer rollout with opt-in via header, 2) add a streaming gap alert (p99 chunk-gap > 1s), 3) doc note about proxies and client transports.
miguel (infra): I'll add the edge metric and set an alert. Also planning a canary for the improved heuristic with runtime flags.
jess (support): I'll update the ticket and send an incident-like summary to the customer. Emily, sorry for the disruption; tracking as SEV-2 until we complete the safe rollout.
emily (customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please let me know when rollout is stable.
